summary: Wire the canonical classify_node discriminator into the PRODUCTION interface path so FunctionInfo.kind is populated (additive) for Lua/Luau functions. Lua is the minimal Stage-3 case: it has NO native class/method/macro surface, so the ONLY construct classify_node soundly classifies is a plain function (function_declaration / function_definition_statement -> EntityKind::Function). Single source of truth: crate::ast::entity::classify_node / EntityKind::Function. No new per-language kind table. The Lua table-convention 'class' keeps its heuristic kind:"table" (NOT expressible via classify_node; deliberately preserved — no class kind invented for tables).

scope_notes: Lua has no class/method/macro/trait/enum native surface. classify_node(Lua) supports ONLY Function. Per the task spec, kind is populated ONLY for what classify_node soundly supports; no class kind is invented for the table convention.

The Lua table-convention class (extract.classes M -> kind:"table") is a synthetic construct assembled from multiple table-qualified function declarations — there is NO single AST node classify_node can classify, and "table" is not an EntityKind variant. Routing it through classify_node would regress it, so it is intentionally left untouched.

interface routes the export `new = M.new` to values[] (the module-symbol table does not track the table-qualified static method M.new as a top-level function) — pre-existing behaviour, unrelated to this additive-kind change. The genuine top-level functions helper/compute are the function-axis carriers.

structure's method/function distinction for Lua (is_lua_table_qualified_function) is structural and cannot be expressed by classify_node (which sees function_declaration for both forms); it is therefore left as-is to avoid regressing the method kind. structure already agrees with classify_node on plain functions (kind=function).
